page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-2GB is a lightweight entry-tier virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 2 shared vCPUs mapped to AMD EPYC 9575F processors operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 2.0 GB of system memory (1.0 GB per core), 30 GB of local SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU feature set includes AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, and AVX-512_BF16) and standard cryptographic instructions (AES, VAES, SHA-NI), but omits hardware accelerator units or GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded execution derived from the modern AMD EPYC microarchitecture. In stress-ng single-core tests, the instance scored 3,883.68, placing it in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 39.79 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reached 16.76 GB/sec, both ranking in the top tier. Memory bandwidth achieves 418.11 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached blocks and 61.74 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads.

Performance tradeoffs become evident in multi-threaded and aggregate throughput metrics due to the low total core count and shared CPU allocation. Stress-ng multi-core testing placed within the middle 50% with 7,762.75 points, while the aggregate PassMark CPU score of 6,494.94 and PassMark memory score of 915.43 ranked in the lower percentiles. Redis SET operations measured 5.67 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations reached 2,196.38, reflecting the overall constraints of a 2-vCPU, 2.0 GB profile.

Cost efficiency is focused on low-overhead baseline utility, bundling local SSD storage with modern CPU instruction support. UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-2GB is best suited for entry-level workloads including static web serving, lightweight automation scripts, low-traffic edge gateways, and small utility background tasks that require modern x86 instructions but modest memory footprints.

Built on x86_64 architecture via the KVM hypervisor, it includes AVX-512 vector support and standard cryptographic flags, without GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core CPU throughput and compression rates, balanced by average multi-core and memory subsystem metrics due to core and capacity limits. Static web serving achieves 9.62 GB/sec throughput, while database and memory benchmark scores fall into lower percentiles. The configuration is best suited for small web services, development environments, and low-memory background tasks.
